final_candidates.decision_summary: Best structure compatibility (0.942) with the strongest PLM (0.155) and MSA (0.325) support among all candidates, indicating a folding-stabilizing, evolutionarily tolerated substitution. Rank 1 across all evidence dimensions.
Good structure compatibility (0.717) and moderate PLM (0.227) despite near-zero MSA frequency. Helix-stabilizing Thr substitution retained as rank 2.
Conservative charge-preserving alternative at the most evolutionarily plastic position, where the backbone tolerates substitution. No direct tool evaluation of Q, so confidence stays below K264N.

stop_reason.detail: Max agent rounds and tool budget reached; additional evidence could not change the Top-3.

history.rationale: This threonine-to-isoleucine stem-adjacent substitution is analogous to HA-stabilizing mutations in other influenza A subtypes that strengthen the prefusion trimer interface. It is also conservative enough to plausibly retain folding and function.
Lowest structure score of the pool and very low PLM/MSA support. Demoted; near rejection.
Structure score is only moderate while both PLM (0.024) and MSA (0.012) strongly disfavor the mutation; unlikely to beat the remaining candidates.

rejection.reason: Structure score is only moderate while both PLM (0.024) and MSA (0.012) strongly disfavor the mutation; unlikely to beat the remaining candidates.

history.rationale: R321 lies near the HA1/HA2 stem-stabilizing region, where hydrophobic substitutions have improved prefusion stability in related HAs. Replacing a solvent-exposed arginine with isoleucine may reduce destabilizing buried charge in the prefusion state.

Best structure score (0.83) but zero evolutionary tolerance and near-zero ESM-1v plausibility; charged-to-hydrophobic swap at a conserved site risks function. Demoted but retained as structure-favored option.
Good structural compatibility but zero PLM plausibility and zero homolog frequency suggest the substitution is not naturally tolerated; demoted below the K264 hedged pair.
Despite the highest structure delta, both PLM (0.000) and MSA (0.000) strongly disfavor it, suggesting the fixed-backbone score is overconfident. Reject.

rejection.reason: Despite the highest structure delta, both PLM (0.000) and MSA (0.000) strongly disfavor it, suggesting the fixed-backbone score is overconfident. Reject.

history.rationale: V166N creates an N-X-T sequon at an exposed HA1 head loop, and added N-linked glycans often improve HA folding efficiency and environmental persistence. The site is outside canonical catalytic or disulfide features.
Zero homolog frequency and low PLM despite acceptable structure score; high B-factor region also weakens structural evidence. Rejected.

rejection.reason: Zero homolog frequency and low PLM despite acceptable structure score; high B-factor region also weakens structural evidence. Rejected.

history.rationale: K264N would create an N-X-S glycosylation sequon in a surface loop, potentially increasing glycan-mediated stability. Lysine-to-asparagine here is structurally plausible but needs compatibility and conservation checks.
Only candidate supported by all three tools: positive ProteinMPNN delta, moderate ESM-1v plausibility, and 32% homolog frequency (evolutionary tolerance). Promoted to rank 1.
K264N is the only candidate supported by all three dimensions (structure 0.942, PLM 0.155, MSA 0.325), consistent with a stability-neutral-to-positive, evolutionarily tolerated substitution.
Best structure score (0.942) with the strongest PLM and MSA support among remaining candidates; K264 appears evolutionarily plastic. Remains rank 1.

A372 is in the HA2 stem region, where threonine may increase local hydrogen bonding and has precedent as a tolerated seasonal HA substitution. It is a moderate candidate for improving prefusion stability.
Consistent weak-to-moderate support across all three tools (0.72 structure, 0.23 PLM, small but nonzero MSA frequency). Promoted to rank 2 as a balanced low-risk substitution.
Solid structure and highest PLM plausibility among remaining candidates, but near-zero MSA frequency lowers confidence; retained pending functional-annotation check for epitope/glycosylation context.
Good structure compatibility and moderate PLM despite near-zero MSA frequency; a helix-stabilizing Thr substitution. Retain as rank 2.

S143N would create an N-X-S glycosylation motif in a head-surface serine-rich loop, potentially adding a stabilizing glycan. However, antigenic effects and glycosylation-site feasibility must be evaluated.

The structure tool reports a WT mismatch at the mapped residue, meaning S143N does not match the sequence/backbone numbering and the candidate is likely invalid as stated. Rejecting pending any re-check.

rejection.reason: The structure tool reports a WT mismatch at the mapped residue, meaning S143N does not match the sequence/backbone numbering and the candidate is likely invalid as stated. Rejecting pending any re-check.

history.rationale: K264 shows the highest evolutionary plasticity and a positive structure delta for N; Q is a conservative charge-preserving alternative likely also tolerated. Added as a hedged sibling candidate for the same position.
Same high-plasticity position as K264N with conservative charge-neutral change; structure/MSA evidence at the position transfers partially, promoting it above R321I.
Hedged conservative alternative at the most plastic position; no direct evidence yet, so confidence stays below K264N. Retain as rank 3.
